subject: science
passage: Along parts of the Pacific coast of North America, purple sea urchins multiplied rapidly in the mid-2010s, after a wasting disease killed most of the sunflower sea stars that prey on them. Freed from their main predator, the urchins grazed once-dense kelp forests down to bare rock, creating what ecologists call "urchin barrens." At some monitored sites off northern California, the number of urchins on each square meter of seafloor, once only a handful, ______ to several dozen, and the kelp has not returned.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject is "the number," a singular noun; "of urchins on each square meter of seafloor" and "once only a handful" only describe it. "The number of" takes a singular verb (unlike "a number of," which means "several" and takes a plural verb). The present perfect "has risen" also matches the present-tense "has not returned."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Have risen" is plural; it seems to agree with "urchins," but the subject is the singular "number."
explanation.B: Correct. The singular verb "has risen" agrees with the subject "the number."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Are rising" is plural, so it doesn't agree with the singular subject "the number."
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Rise" is plural, so it doesn't agree with the singular subject "the number."
